issues.body: `keyword_hints` starts a candidate at any ASCII letter whose immediately preceding byte is not accepted by the ASCII-only `is_ident_char`. In a valid SPARQL variable containing non-ASCII name characters (for example an ASCII typo-like suffix after `é`) the preceding UTF-8 byte is treated as a delimiter, so the suffix can be reported as a keyword typo. The same problem applies after a PN_LOCAL escape such as a backslash in a valid prefixed-name local. This contradicts the public contract that every valid query returns an empty vector and makes the public helper noisy on legal SPARQL syntax. The valid-query test exercises only ASCII names, so it does not establish that contract.
issues.fix_hint: Tokenize according to the vendored parser's SPARQL lexical rules, or at minimum make candidate-boundary detection aware of Unicode PN/VARNAME characters and PN_LOCAL escapes. Add real-parser-backed regression tests using valid Unicode variable names and escaped prefixed-name locals whose ASCII suffix is close to a keyword, asserting both that parsing succeeds and that `keyword_hints` is empty.
issues.title: Valid Unicode and escaped identifiers can produce keyword hints

verdict.summary: The non-rewriting integration and failure-path test are sound, but the public diagnostic does not meet its documented guarantee of returning no hints for every valid query. Its ASCII-only standalone-token check can interpret ASCII substrings inside valid non-ASCII variables or escaped prefixed-name locals as bare keyword typos. The current tests cover only ASCII identifiers and therefore miss the load-bearing false-positive case.
